text.title: Conversion Tracking Procedure
text.summary: Eight steps from the destination list to a QA-verified tracking config: register the event taxonomy in events.yml and wire the CI validator, name events inside the GA4 limits, give monetary events their transaction_id, push Consent Mode v2 defaults before the config call, put the server container on a first-party subdomain forwarding the browser identifiers, write the dual-send dedup, strip PII and hash matching identifiers, then run the fixtures in three browsers plus an ad-blocker profile and validate.

step.name: register-the-event-taxonomy
step.input: The business events the site must report; the destinations (GA4, Google Ads, Meta, Plausible).
step.action: Write `site_domain` and `destinations` in `templates/conversion-tracking.config.yaml`. Create `events.yml` with one entry per event: name, required parameters and the conversion role per destination. Add `templates/validate-events.py` to CI and set `registry.enforced_in_ci: true`.
step.decision-gate: No destination exists: stop, nothing to track into (06-decision-tree.xml). CI does not fail on an unregistered name: fix the pipeline before any tag code merges (r-event-registry-single-source).

step.name: name-events-inside-the-ga4-limits
step.action: Make every `name` snake_case, at most 40 characters, with no `google_`, `ga_`, `firebase_` or `_` prefix; use the exact recommended name (`purchase`, `sign_up`, `generate_lead`, `add_to_cart`) with `recommended: true`. List at most 25 `parameters` per event, names at most 40 characters, `max_string_length` at most 100.
step.decision-gate: A synonym such as `order_completed` or `signup` appears: rename to the recommended event (r-ga4-naming-and-parameter-limits).

step.name: give-monetary-events-a-transaction-id
step.input: Events with revenue; the order system's order identifier.
step.action: Set `monetary: true` and add `value` (number), `currency` (ISO 4217) and `transaction_id` (the order id) to `parameters`; set `dedup.event_id_field: transaction_id` and `shared_across_destinations: true` so the same id is the Meta `event_id` and the Google Ads `transaction_id`.
step.decision-gate: A revenue event has no order identifier: it is not sent until it does (r-monetary-conversion-carries-transaction-id).

step.name: push-consent-defaults-before-config
step.input: The consent management platform; the markets served.
step.action: Set `consent.mode: v2`, `defaults_before_config: true`, the four `signals`, one `regional_defaults[]` entry per region (denied for consent jurisdictions, `region` parameter set), and `server_honours_consent: true`. Place `gtag('consent', 'default', ...)` before `gtag('config', ...)` in the snippet.
step.decision-gate: The default push arrives after the first hit, or the server container ignores consent: the implementation is non-compliant (r-consent-state-before-any-tag).

step.name: serve-the-server-container-first-party
step.input: DNS control for the site domain; the GTM server container or Cloudflare Worker.
step.action: Set `server_side.enabled: true`, `endpoint` to a subdomain of `site_domain` (for example `gtm.example.com`), `cookies_http_only: true`, `forwards` with `_fbp`, `_fbc`, `client_id` and `session_id`, `client_id_source: _ga cookie`, `fresh_ids_generated: false`.
step.decision-gate: The container runs on the vendor default domain: Safari still treats it as third-party; move it before enabling any server send (r-server-endpoint-first-party-domain, r-browser-server-dedup-and-identifiers).

step.name: write-the-dual-send-dedup
step.action: For each such event set `dedup.event_id_field` (the `transaction_id` for monetary events, an `event_id` parameter otherwise) and `shared_across_destinations: true`; the server copy reuses the browser's id and event name.
step.decision-gate: The server mints its own id: every purchase counts twice in Ads Manager and every server hit becomes a new GA4 user (r-browser-server-dedup-and-identifiers).

step.name: strip-pii-and-hash-matching-identifiers
step.input: `events[].parameters`; confirmation-page URLs; the ad platforms' matching parameters.
step.action: Mark every parameter `pii: false`; remove identifying query parameters before `page_view` fires; for matching identifiers (`em`, `ph`) normalise, SHA-256 hash and set `hashed: true`. Write a PII-free `example_payload` per fixture.
step.decision-gate: An example payload contains an `@` or a phone-shaped string: the validator rejects it (r-no-pii-in-parameters).

step.name: run-the-fixtures-and-validate
step.input: The change under review; Chrome, Safari, Firefox and a Chrome profile with a mainstream ad blocker.
step.action: Set `qa.change_ref`, `browsers`, `adblock_profile: true`. For every event add a fixture with `expected_parameters` and one `results[]` row per browser (including `chrome_adblock`) per destination the event targets. Run `scripts/validate-conversion-tracking.py --file`.
step.decision-gate: An event has no fixture, or a browser or destination has no result row: the change does not merge (r-qa-fixtures-per-tracking-change).

list.item: Config validates via `scripts/validate-conversion-tracking.py` with no violation.
Every monetary event carries `transaction_id` shared across destinations, and every dual-sent event has a dedup block.
Every event has fixture results for three browsers plus the ad-blocker profile on every destination it targets.
